business_flows.flow_name: Guest Checkout Journey (includes an authenticated Login step)
business_flows.description: A single linear journey recorded under one ThreadGroup ('Guest Checkout Users', 50 threads / 60s ramp-up): land on the home page, log in, search for a product, view its detail page, add it to cart, apply a coupon, submit shipping information, and place the order. Despite the 'Guest Checkout' naming on the TestPlan and ThreadGroup, the recording contains a real Login step with a username/password, which is not typical of a guest (non-authenticated) checkout. There is no logout or session-end step; the recording stops right after order placement.

risk_flags: ThreadGroup is named 'Guest Checkout Users' and the TestPlan 'Magento Guest Checkout', but the recording includes an authenticated Login step (POST /customer/account/loginPost/ with username+password) -- this doesn't match a typical guest (non-authenticated) checkout. Confirm with the user whether Login belongs in this flow or was captured by mistake.

No CookieManager element is present in the JMX -- session/cookie handling across Login -> Checkout Flow isn't explicitly configured in the recording. If the target app relies on a session cookie in addition to form_key/quoteId, this needs to be added when the runnable test is built.
No logout / session-end step -- the recording ends immediately after Place Order; session cleanup behavior under load is untested.

Single ThreadGroup ('Guest Checkout Users', 50 threads / 60s ramp-up) -- only one user journey/type was recorded, so realistic task-mix weighting (e.g. % of users who apply a coupon) can't be inferred from this recording alone and should be confirmed with the user.

Shipping address and payment method are hardcoded literal values inside raw JSON bodies, not wired to any CSV variable -- every virtual user would submit an identical address and payment method unless these are parameterized before load testing.

Search keyword ('running shoes') and the PDP product id ('12345') are single hardcoded values not declared in the existing users.csv CSVDataSet (which only lists username, password, sku, quantity, coupon_code) -- they aren't varying at all today and need their own test-data columns, kept in sync with sku.

All hit_count values are 1 (a single-iteration recording) -- can't infer relative step popularity (e.g. coupon usage rate) from hit counts; get real traffic ratios from the user before weighting tasks.
2 noise requests were filtered out (1 static CSS asset, 1 Google Analytics beacon) of 10 total observed -- a small, unremarkable amount, included for completeness.
